a: Japan — Geology — Table 11. Seismic Record in Japan (pre-Tokugawa period)
t: An area of 8—10 sq. kilometres in Tosa subsided and was covered by sea-water.

a: Japan — Geology — Table 11. Seismic Record in Japan (pre-Tokugawa period)
t: Earthquake with tidal waves visited Mutsu and about 1,000 people were killed.

a: Japan — Geology — Table 11. Seismic Record in Japan (pre-Tokugawa period)
t: Earthquakes in districts round about Kyoto.

a: Japan — Geology — Table 11. Seismic Record in Japan (pre-Tokugawa period)
t: Tokaido was visited by a severe earthquake, causing death of over 5,000 persons. Hamana lagoon (Maizaka station, Tokaido Railway, formerly inland lake) was formed.

a: Japan — Geology — Table 11. Seismic Record in Japan (pre-Tokugawa period)
t: Bungo (Kyushu) was visited by a severe earthquake and 708 persons killed.

a: Japan — Geology — Table 11. Seismic Record in Japan (pre-Tokugawa period)
t: Districts about Kyoto was shaken and 1,200 persons killed.

a: Manchoukuo — National Defence — Table 4. Chronology of Bandit Suppression by the Manchoukuo Army
t: Suppression of Anti-Kirin Troops. No. of enemy forces: 20,000; No. of Manchoukuo forces: 7,000. Forces: Manchoukuo: Kirin Army & River Patrol Fleet. Comdr. Gen. Yu Shen-chang. The Enemy: Anti-Kirin Troops. Leaders. Li Ting Tiao, etc. Remarks: The Manchoukuo Army cooperating with the Japanese Forces, drove back the Anti-Kirin Troops to the northern part of Kirin Prov., secured the water routes of the Sungari River and regained Iran-hsien.

a: Manchoukuo — National Defence — Table 4. Chronology of Bandit Suppression by the Manchoukuo Army
t: 1st Pacification of the Tungpien-Tao Region. No. of enemy forces: 20,000; No. of Manchoukuo forces: 4,000. Forces: Manchoukuo: Fengtien Army. Comdr. Gen. Yu Chi-shan. The Enemy: North Eastern People Salvation Army & Ta-ta-hui (Big Sword League). Leaders. Tang Tsu-wu & Wang Feng-ke. Remarks: Tang Tsu-wu revolted and attacked the Japanese Consulate at Tunghua. The Fengtien Army cooperating with the Japanese Police Corps, tried to drive the bandits but were repulsed.

a: Manchoukuo — National Defence — Table 4. Chronology of Bandit Suppression by the Manchoukuo Army
t: Suppression of Ma Chan-shan. No. of enemy forces: 16,000; No. of Manchoukuo forces: 5,000. Forces: Manchoukuo: Heilungkiang Army cooperating with the Japanese Army. Comdr. Cheng Chin-yuan. The Enemy: Ma Chan-shan Troops & Li Bandits. Leaders. Ma Chan-shan & Li Hai-ching. Remarks: Ma Chan-shan escaping from Tsitsihar in April, gathered his troops again and revolted. The Manchoukuo Army sent two troops and attacked his headquarters at Hailin, cooperating with the Japanese Army.

a: Manchoukuo — National Defence — Table 4. Chronology of Bandit Suppression by the Manchoukuo Army
t: Suppression of Li Hai-ching. No. of enemy forces: 10,000; No. of Manchoukuo forces: 6,000. Forces: Manchoukuo: Heilungkiang, Kirin and Taoliao Army assisted by the Japanese Air Corps. The Enemy: A part of Ma Chan-shan's Troops & Li Bandits. Leaders. Li Hai-ching. Remarks: Bandit Li occupying the southern part of Heilungkiang Province and Fuyu of Kirin Province, took sway of the district. The Manchoukuo Army attacked the bandits with the aid of the Japanese air corps.

a: Manchoukuo — National Defence — Table 4. Chronology of Bandit Suppression by the Manchoukuo Army
t: Punitive expedition against Feng Chan-hai near Yushou (Kirin). No. of enemy forces: 15,000; No. of Manchoukuo forces: 1,000. Forces: Manchoukuo: Kirin Army. The Enemy: Anti-Kirin Troops. Leaders. Feng Chan-hai & Kung Chang-hai. Remarks: Anti-Kirin Troops gathered in the south of Harbin. The Manchoukuo Army encountered the enemy near Ssuhocheng (Pinkiang), but were repulsed.

a: Manchoukuo — National Defence — Table 4. Chronology of Bandit Suppression by the Manchoukuo Army
t: Suppression of remaining bandits of Li Hai-ching troops. No. of enemy forces: 2,000; No. of Manchoukuo forces: 1,500. Forces: Manchoukuo: Heilungkiang Army. Comdr. Major-Gen. Feng Kuan-you. The Enemy: Remaining bandits of Li Hai-ching. Remarks: The Manchoukuo Army attacked the remaining bandits and killed 50 and captured 2 chiefs.

a: Manchoukuo — National Defence — Table 4. Chronology of Bandit Suppression by the Manchoukuo Army
t: 1st punitive expedition against Feng Chan-hai. No. of enemy forces: 15,000; No. of Manchoukuo forces: 7,000. Forces: Manchoukuo: Taoliao & Kirin Army cooperating with the Japanese Army. The Enemy: Anti-Kirin Troops. Leaders. Feng Chan-hai & Kung Chang-hai. Remarks: The Manchoukuo Army pacified Shuangcheng, Acheng, Yushou, Wuchang, and Shulan Districts.

a: Manchoukuo — National Defence — Table 4. Chronology of Bandit Suppression by the Manchoukuo Army
t: Punitive expedition against Mongolian Bandits. No. of enemy forces: 2,000; No. of Manchoukuo forces: 2,500. Forces: Manchoukuo: Taoliao Army. Comdr. Major-Gen. Tang Yu-lin. The Enemy: Mongolian Bandits. Leaders. Hu Pao-shan, Hei Pao-tao, and Li Pao-ting. Remarks: The Mongolian bandits occupied Chanyu-hsien and destroyed the railway. The Manchoukuo Army cooperating with the Japanese Army, attacked the enemy and recovered Chanyu-hsien.

a: Manchoukuo — National Defence — Table 4. Chronology of Bandit Suppression by the Manchoukuo Army
t: Attack on Tien-chien bandits at Shuangcheng (Pinkiang). No. of enemy forces: 3,500; No. of Manchoukuo forces: 700. Forces: Manchoukuo: Kirin Army. The Enemy: Tien Chen Bandits. Leader. Tien Chen. Remarks: The Tien Chen bandits besieged Shuangcheng but were driven away by the Manchoukuo Army.

a: Manchoukuo — National Defence — Table 4. Chronology of Bandit Suppression by the Manchoukuo Army
t: 2nd punitive expedition against Feng Chan-hai. No. of enemy forces: 10,000; No. of Manchoukuo forces: 7,000. Forces: Manchoukuo: Kirin Army. The Enemy: Anti-Kirin Troops. Leaders. Feng Chan-hai & Kung Chang-hai. Remarks: Finding that the Feng Chan-hai bandits were moving to Jehol Province, the Manchoukuo Army besieged them in Kirin-Changchun District, but the enemy escaped to Jehol through Nungan district.

a: Manchoukuo — National Defence — Table 4. Chronology of Bandit Suppression by the Manchoukuo Army
t: Suppression of Su Ping-wen at Hailar. No. of enemy forces: 20,000; No. of Manchoukuo forces: 4,500. Forces: Manchoukuo: Heilungkiang Army & Hsingan South Provincial Guards cooperating with the Japanese Army. The Enemy: Su Ping-wen Troops. Leaders. Su Ping-wen & Chang Tien-chiu. Remarks: Su Ping-wen revolted and the Manchouli Incident occured. The Manchoukuo Army cooperating with the Japanese Army, engaged in battle at Fulaluchi. Su Ping-wen fled into Russia after being defeated.

a: Manchoukuo — National Defence — Table 4. Chronology of Bandit Suppression by the Manchoukuo Army
t: 2nd pacification of the Tungpien-Tao Region. No. of enemy forces: 20,000; No. of Manchoukuo forces: 8,000. Forces: Manchoukuo: Fengtien Army. The Enemy: North Eastern People Salvation Army. Leader. Tang Tsu-wu. Remarks: The Manchoukuo Army made an expedition into The Tungpien-Tao Region with the Japanese Army. 1,000 bandits surrendered and 270 were killed.

a: Manchoukuo — National Defence — Table 4. Chronology of Bandit Suppression by the Manchoukuo Army
t: Punitive expedition against Li Hai-ching. No. of enemy forces: 3,000; No. of Manchoukuo forces: 3,500. Forces: Manchoukuo: Heilungkiang Army. The Enemy: Li Hai-ching Bandits. Leader. Li Hai-ching. Remarks: The Manchoukuo Army engaged the Li bandits which were to attack the Manchoukuo & Japanese Army from the rear in response to Su Ping-wen, and drove them into Jehol Province.

a: Manchoukuo — National Defence — Table 4. Chronology of Bandit Suppression by the Manchoukuo Army
t: Pacification of middle territory bebetween Kirin and Hailung. No. of enemy forces: 5,000; No. of Manchoukuo forces: 5,000. Forces: Manchoukuo: Fengtien & Kirin Army cooperating with the Japanese Army. The Enemy: Professional bandits including Communist Bandits. Leaders. San Kiang-hao, Tien Chen, Sung Kuo-jung, etc. Remarks: The Manchoukuo Army cooperated with the Japanese Army in pacifying the middle land between Kirin and Hailung.

a: Manchoukuo — National Defence — Table 4. Chronology of Bandit Suppression by the Manchoukuo Army
t: 3rd pacification of the Tungpien-Tao Region. No. of enemy forces: 2,000; No. of Manchoukuo forces: 5,000. Forces: Manchoukuo: Fengtien Army. The Enemy: Professional bandits. Remarks: The Manchoukuo Army pacified the district and disarmed 1,800 bandits.

a: Manchoukuo — National Defence — Table 4. Chronology of Bandit Suppression by the Manchoukuo Army
t: Subjugation of Jehol Province. No. of enemy forces: 130,000; No. of Manchoukuo forces: 42,000. Forces: Manchoukuo: Taoliao Army and other troops cooperating with the Japanese Army. Comdr. Gen. Chang Ching-hui & Lieut.-Gen. Kuo En-lin. The Enemy: Tang Yu-lin Troops, etc. Leader. Tang Yu-lin. Remarks: The Manchoukuo Army engaged in the subjugation of Jehol with the Japanese Army, pacified the Province, and drove away the Anti-Manchoukuo troops out of the Great Wall.

a: Manchoukuo — National Defence — Table 4. Chronology of Bandit Suppression by the Manchoukuo Army
t: Pacification of western side of Liao River. No. of enemy forces: 600; No. of Manchoukuo forces: 900. Forces: Manchoukuo: Fengtien Army. Comdr. Gen. Yu Chi-shan. The Enemy: Professional bandits. Leader. Lu Shih-chieh, Pei Pa-tien, Li Hua-i, etc. Remarks: The bandits under Lu Shih-chieh, invaded the western part of the Liao River to disorder the inland with a view to moving into the eastern part of the Liao River Region. The Manchoukuo Army attacked them for 4 months, and exterminated most of them, and dispersed the remainder.

a: Manchoukuo — National Defence — Table 4. Chronology of Bandit Suppression by the Manchoukuo Army
t: Punitive expedition into Kirin Province. No. of enemy forces: 20,000; No. of Manchoukuo forces: 35,000. Forces: Manchoukuo: Kirin. Heilungkiang and other troops cooperating with the Japanese Army. The Enemy: Professional bandits in Kirin Province. Remarks: The Manchoukuo Army cooperating with the Japanese Army, pacified Kirin Province. Wang Tien-chen and 2 other chiefs were killed, and many bandits surrendered or were exterminated.

a: Manchoukuo — National Defence — Table 4. Chronology of Bandit Suppression by the Manchoukuo Army
t: 4th pacification of the Tungpien-Tao Region. No. of enemy forces: 4,000; No. of Manchoukuo forces: 5,000. Forces: Manchoukuo: 1st District Army. Comdr. Lieut.-Gen. Liao Pi-chen. The Enemy: Professional bandits including Korean Bandits in Tungpien-Tao Region. Leaders. Kung Wen, Wang Tien-yang, Wang Feng-ke, etc. Remarks: Bandits in the Tungpien-Tao Region commenced activity after the Japanese Army centralized its troops stationed in small detachments in the country. The Manchoukuo Army, cooperating with the Japanese forces, gathered at Tungho, attacked and subjugated the bandits, and confiscated their arms.

a: Manchoukuo — National Defence — Table 4. Chronology of Bandit Suppression by the Manchoukuo Army
t: Summer expedition into East Kirin Province. No. of enemy forces: 1,500; No. of Manchoukuo forces: 250. Forces: Manchoukuo: 2nd District Army. Comdr. Major-Gen. Chin En-kuei. The Enemy: North Eastern People's Revolutionary Troops. Leaders. Wu I-ching, Ching Shan, etc. Remarks: The Manchoukuo Army cooperating with the Japanese Army, attacked the bandits gathering near Lake Kingpofu (Sankiang), and drove them into the mountains and overthrew their headquarters.

a: Manchoukuo — National Defence — Table 4. Chronology of Bandit Suppression by the Manchoukuo Army
t: Pacification of Antu (Chientao). No. of enemy forces: 3,000; No. of Manchoukuo forces: 300. Forces: Manchoukuo: 2nd District Army cooperating with the Japanese Army. Comdr. Major-Gen. Takeo Hino. The Enemy: Professional bandits. Leaders. Tai Wen-Yuan, Tao Chen-shan, etc. Remarks: The Manchoukuo Army preserved peace in Antu-hsien when bandits attacked the district.

a: Manchoukuo — National Defence — Table 4. Chronology of Bandit Suppression by the Manchoukuo Army
t: 1st pacification of Yenki District (Chientao). No. of enemy forces: 1,000; No. of Manchoukuo forces: 1,000. Forces: Manchoukuo: 2nd District Army cooperating with the Japanese Army. Comdr. Major-Gen. Chin En-kuei. The Enemy: Norh Eastern People's Revolutionary Troops. Leaders. Chu Chen, Pe Chun, etc. Remarks: The Manchoukuo Army cooperating with the Japanese Army, overthrew the headquarters of the Communist bandits, and despatched forces to several places to oppress the operation of bandits and to help the farmers to get their crops.

a: Manchoukuo — National Defence — Table 4. Chronology of Bandit Suppression by the Manchoukuo Army
t: Summer expedition to the West Kirin-Fengtien Frontier. No. of enemy forces: 800; No. of Manchoukuo forces: 1,300. Forces: Manchoukuo: 2nd District Army cooperating with the Japanese Army. Comdr. Lieut.-Gen. Hsing Shih-lien. The Enemy: Professional bandits including Communist Bandits. Leaders. Tien Hu, Ma Tuan, etc. Remarks: The Manchoukuo Army pacified the western part of Kirin Province with the Japanese Army and subjugated most of the bandits there.

a: Manchoukuo — National Defence — Table 4. Chronology of Bandit Suppression by the Manchoukuo Army
t: 5th pacification of the Tungpien-Tao Region. No. of enemy forces: 4,500; No. of Manchoukuo forces: 6,000. Forces: Manchoukuo: 1st District Army cooperating with the Japanese Army. Comdr. Lieut.-Gen. Liao Pi-chen. The Enemy: Professional bandits in Tungpien-Tao Region. Leaders. Wang Tien-yang, Wang Feng-ke, Ma Tuan, Tien Hu, etc. Remarks: The Manchoukuo Army cooperated with the Japanese Army in suppressing the bandits, and established the PAO CHIA system and improved the communications network.

a: Manchoukuo — National Defence — Table 4. Chronology of Bandit Suppression by the Manchoukuo Army
t: Blockade of Eastern Frontier & Japan-Manchou Joint Autumn Pacification of Kirin, the Tungpien-Tao Region and Pinkiang & Sankiang Provinces. No. of enemy forces: 12,000; No. of Manchoukuo forces: 19,600. Forces: Manchoukuo: 1st, 2nd and 4th District Army cooperating With the Japanese Army. Comdr. Gen. Yu Chi-shan, Gen. Kie Hsing and Major-Gen. Wang Tsi-chung. The Enemy: Professional and other bandits in Kirin, Tungpien-Tao, and other Districts. Leaders. Sieh Wen-tung, Tien Hu, Wang Tien-yang, etc. Remarks: The Manchoukuo Army gathered its forces in Kirin Province, and commenced an autumnal expedition and blockaded the Eastern Frontier to make effective their operation. The expedition was ended in November, but the blockade was carried on. (In this period, each Army District made a punitive expedition in several district.)

a: Manchoukuo — National Defence — Table 4. Chronology of Bandit Suppression by the Manchoukuo Army
t: Winter expedition into Iran District (Sankiang). No. of enemy forces: 1,300; No. of Manchoukuo forces: 900. Forces: Manchoukuo: 4th District Army. Comdr. Major-Gen. Liu Wei-hun. The Enemy: Anti-Manchoukuo Bandits. Leaders. Sieh Wen-tung, etc. Remarks: The bandits under Sieh Wen-tung, were active in Iran & Poli districts. The Manchoukuo Army attacked them and drove them to the southwest.

a: Manchoukuo — National Defence — Table 4. Chronology of Bandit Suppression by the Manchoukuo Army
t: Winter expedition into Yenki District (Chientao). No. of enemy forces: 700; No. of Manchoukuo forces: 500. Forces: Manchoukuo: 4th District Army cooperating with the Japanese Army. Comdr. Major-Gen. Chin En-kuei. The Enemy: Professional bandits including Communist Bandits. Leaders Pe Chun, Hai Lung, etc. Remarks: The Manchoukuo Army cooperating with the Japanese Army, attacked the bandits in Yenki district, and overthrew their headquarters.

a: Manchoukuo — National Defence — Table 4. Chronology of Bandit Suppression by the Manchoukuo Army
t: Winter expedition into Lotsukou (Chientao). No. of enemy forces: 1,000; No. of Manchoukuo forces: 1,200. Forces: Manchoukuo: Chin-an Army & 4th Distric Army cooperating with the Japanese Army. Comdr. Major-Gen. Juzaburo Fujii. The Enemy: North East Volunteer Troops. Leaders. Kung Hsien-jung, etc. Remarks: The Manchoukuo Army cooperating with the Japanese Army, attacked the bandits in Yenki district, and overthrew their headquarters. The Manchoukuo Army attacked the bandits under Kung Hsien-jung, who disordered the Eastern Frontier and were preparing for further raids in the north mountains of Lotsukou (Chientao), and overthrew their headquarters after one month's hard fighting.

a: Manchoukuo — National Defence — Table 4. Chronology of Bandit Suppression by the Manchoukuo Army
t: Winter expedition into Pinkiang District. No. of enemy forces: 1,800; No. of Manchoukuo forces: 900. Forces: Manchoukuo: 2nd District Army. Comdr. Major-Gen. Li Wen-lung. The Enemy: Anti-Manchoukuo Bandits. Leaders. Teh Lin, etc. Remarks: The Manchoukuo Army attacked the bandits under Teh Lin, which devastated Wuchang-hsien, and heavily oppressed them.

a: Manchoukuo — National Defence — Table 4. Chronology of Bandit Suppression by the Manchoukuo Army
t: Winter expedition into Pinkiang District. No. of enemy forces: 1,600; No. of Manchoukuo forces: 1,100. Forces: Manchoukuo: 2nd District Army. Comdr. Major-Gen. Wang Tsu-chen. The Enemy: Anti-Manchoukuo Bandits. Leaders. Chao Shang-chih, etc. Remarks: The Manchoukuo Army attacked the Anti-Manchoukuo Bandits which were devastating the north district of the N.M.R., and overthrew their headquarters.

a: Manchoukuo — National Defence — Table 4. Chronology of Bandit Suppression by the Manchoukuo Army
t: 6th Winter pacification of the Tungpien-Tao Region. No. of enemy forces: 4,000; No. of Manchoukuo forces: 6,000. Forces: Manchoukuo: 1st District Army. Comdr. Lieut.-Gen. Wang Tien-chung. The Enemy: Professional bandits including Communist Bandits. Leaders. Wang Feng-ke, Ma Tuan, Tien Hu, etc (Wang Tien-yang killed). Remarks: The Manchoukuo Army attacked the Communist Bandits in the mountainous districts and drove them to the Frontier of Chosen.

a: Manchoukuo — National Defence — Table 4. Chronology of Bandit Suppression by the Manchoukuo Army
t: Pacification of Chengteh & Chaoyang Districts. (Jehol). No. of enemy forces: 2,700; No. of Manchoukuo forces: 2,200. Forces: Manchoukuo: 5th District Army. Comdr. Lieut.-Gen. Wang Yung-ching. The Enemy: Anti-Manchoukuo Bandits. Leaders. Lan Tien-lin, Wang Kuo-shui, etc. Remarks: The Manchoukuo Army is operating an expedition against the Anti-Manchoukuo Bandits under Lan Tien-lin, which are becoming active in Chengteh & Chaoyang districts.

a: Manchoukuo — National Defence — Table 4. Chronology of Bandit Suppression by the Manchoukuo Army
t: 7th pacification of the Tungpien-Tao Region & expedition to the Kirin-Fengtien Frontier. No. of enemy forces: 3,500; No. of Manchoukuo forces: 6,600. Forces: Manchoukuo: 1st District Army. Comdr. Lieut.-Gen. Liao Pi-chen & Lieut.-Gen. Wang Tien-chung. The Enemy: Professional bandits including Communist Bandits. Leaders. Wang Feng-ke, Ma Tuan, Tien Hu, etc. Remarks: To complete the result of 6th expedition and to overthrew the bandit headquarters, the Manchoukuo Army is operating a punitive expedition in several distrcts.
